reviews.comment: Amazing depth in guiding discussion and selecting applicable and appropriate readings. Get ready to read A LOT, and actually read them not just scanning through the text. Only complaint is he won't grade anything until wayyyyyyy late, after graduation type of late and emailing him is futile.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SUPER easy class.  2 easy tests with one sided cheat sheet.  One 1500 word essay and one 2-3 minute casual video about your essay.  Comment on 15 out of the 26 assigned readings.  And that's it!  Easy grader, responds to emails fast, willing to meet with you on zoom to discuss your essay.  Recommend this class for the creative arts credit

Extremely inaccessible outside class. He rarely responds to emails and delays grading until the last week. With days left in the semester, most assignments remain ungraded. This is unfair to students paying tuition, putting time and effort into assignments, and who need to track their progress. I suggest he gets a TA if he can't be timely.

2 exams, gives answers before them, allows 1 written cheat sheet. 12 HW's, ask 2Q over weeks reading, answer 1Q, 2 essays, 1 video essay, 1 paper. Easy A, not difficult. Attendance is grades by how many times you debate in class through semester (says it once on first day, DONT FORGET, will give out attendance sheet). Easy A, just talk 5x in class.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy and very passionate about what he teaches. Only complaint is that he takes very long to grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Such an amazing teacher! He cares a lot about what he teaches and cares a lot about his students. Takes a while to grade things, but his lectures make the class worth it. Reading quiz due each week, but they are only five questions and he takes the highest 15 out of 22. Take him if you have the opportunity.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Passionate about philosophy but always held class at least 10 minutes after class was over to continue lecture. Did not really grade anything until the last week of school and even then I didn't know my grade until the day final grades were due. Not accessible by email either.

Professor Jaima is a great lecturer and is passionate about philosophy. The course itself is pretty straightforward, and it is easy to do well if you follow his instructions and complete the weekly assignments and semester paper. He was very inaccessible outside of class this semester and did not communicate well.

Amir Jaima is a great professor! He stimulates conversation in class and thoroughly discusses the required readings. Participation from the students is imperative for healthy conversations and interesting debates. He commutes so he's not widely available but he is very helpful when you do need his assistance. Very intriguing man, he wont disappoint

He's super nice, but acts like this class isn't on his priority list. He takes forever to respond to emails and there's four weeks left in the semester and I only have completion grades back. He does essays instead of tests, and the final exam is a take home test. There's a lot of reading and writing but you can skim the readings pretty easily.

Provided a very good introduction to philosophy. He cares about his students and is passionate about the subject. The class is graded based on short weekly writing assignments, two mid-sized essays, and one big paper/presentation. I found it very enjoyable and not too difficult.

I took Dr. Jaima's PHIL 251 class in the honors section and it was one of the best classes I have taken so far. He is tough grader but really wants you to succeed and understand the material. His lectures were interesting and fun. I hope I get the chance to take one of his classes again.
